skill.name: outlook-calendar-automation
skill.description: Automate Outlook Calendar workflows through Rube MCP, including events, attendees, meeting times, invitations, and Teams meeting links.
skill.summary: Guide AI agents through Outlook Calendar scheduling workflows using Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The Markdown file documents Rube MCP workflows for Outlook Calendar and contains no executable Ruby, shell, or local system commands. Most static detections are false positives from inline backticks around tool names, parameters, and fenced examples. The only confirmed risk is the required external MCP endpoint, which means users must trust Rube/Composio and Microsoft OAuth access.

remediation.suggestion: Disclose that users connect to https://rube.app/mcp and must trust Rube, Composio, and Microsoft OAuth permissions before use.

remediation.issue: Calendar actions can notify other people
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating, updating, deleting, declining, or sending invitations through Outlook tools.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Outlook connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `outlook`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `end_datetime`: ISO 8601 end time (must be after start)
- `time_zone`: IANA or Windows timezone (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Pacific Standard Time')
- `attendees_info`: Array of email strings or attendee objects
- `is_html`: Set true if body contains HTML
- `is_online_meeting`: Set true for Teams meeting link
1. `OUTLOOK_GET_MAILBOX_SETTINGS` - Get user timezone for accurate queries [Prerequisite]
3. `OUTLOOK_GET_EVENT` - Get full details for a specific event [Optional]
4. `OUTLOOK_GET_CALENDAR_VIEW` - Get events active during a time window [Alternative]
- `start_datetime`/`end_datetime`: For CALENDAR_VIEW time window (UTC with Z suffix)
- `attendees`: Updated attendee list (replaces existing if provided)
- `body`: Updated description with contentType and content
- `send_notifications`: Send cancellation notices to attendees (default true)
- `attendees`: Array of attendee objects with email and type
- `meetingDuration`: ISO 8601 duration (e.g., 'PT1H' for 1 hour, 'PT30M' for 30 min)
- `StartTime`/`EndTime`: Time window for schedule lookup (max 62 days)
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- time_zone is required and must be a valid IANA or Windows timezone name
- user_id defaults to 'me'; use email or UUID for other users' calendars
- event_id is required; obtain from LIST_EVENTS first
- Valid filter fields: start/dateTime, end/dateTime, subject, categories, isAllDay

content.value_statement: Manual calendar work slows scheduling and increases mistakes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through Outlook workflows using Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Creates Outlook calendar events with subjects, times, locations, attendees, descriptions, and Teams meeting options.
Lists calendars and searches events using Outlook filters, calendar views, sorting, and selected fields.
Updates existing Outlook events after resolving the correct event identifier.
Deletes events or declines invitations with optional comments, responses, and proposed new times.
Finds available meeting times and checks free or busy schedules across attendees.
Handles timezone guidance, OData filter syntax, pagination, and response structure notes.
limitations: Requires a configured Rube MCP server and an active Outlook connection.
Depends on current Rube tool schemas, so the agent must search tools before use.
Calendar actions may send invitations, updates, or cancellation notices to attendees.
The skill provides workflow guidance only and does not include executable automation scripts.

use_cases.title: Schedule Team Meetings
use_cases.description: Create Outlook events with attendees, locations, Teams links, and correct timezone details.

use_cases.title: Find Open Meeting Slots
use_cases.description: Check attendee availability and request meeting time suggestions before sending an invite.

use_cases.title: Maintain Calendar Events
use_cases.description: Search, update, delete, or decline calendar events while preserving the right event context.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Outlook calendar event for [subject] on [date] from [start time] to [end time] in [timezone]. Add [attendees] and confirm before sending invitations.

prompt_templates.title: Find Events by Date
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my Outlook calendar events between [start date and time] and [end date and time]. Use my mailbox timezone, return the most relevant event details, and note any pagination.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Meeting Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Outlook event named [event name] during [date range]. Show the matched event first, then update [fields] only after I confirm the event id and attendee impact.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Group Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Find available meeting times for [attendees] during [time window] for a [duration] meeting. Compare suggestions with free or busy schedules and prepare a confirmed Outlook invite draft.

output_examples.input: Schedule a 30 minute Teams meeting with Dana and Lee tomorrow afternoon.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks the active Outlook connection, searches current Rube tool schemas, finds the user timezone, creates a draft event with a Teams link, and asks before sending invitations.

output_examples.input: Move the project review meeting from Friday morning to Monday at 10 AM.
output_examples.output: The assistant searches matching events, presents the likely event for confirmation, updates the time after approval, and notes that attendees may receive an update.

output_examples.input: Find a one hour slot for the design review next week.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks attendee availability, compares suggested meeting times, reports the best options, and prepares an Outlook event only after the user selects a slot.

best_practices: Call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before each workflow to confirm current Outlook tool schemas.
Resolve timezone and event identifiers before changing or deleting any calendar entry.
Ask for user confirmation before actions that send invites, updates, declines, or cancellations.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a local timezone when Outlook mailbox settings are available.
Do not update attendees without including the full desired attendee list.
Do not delete recurring event masters unless the user confirms all occurrences should be removed.

faq.question: Does this skill require Rube MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on Rube MCP and an active Outlook connection.

faq.question: Can it create Teams meeting links?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the required online meeting settings for Teams for Business links.

faq.question: Can it search my Outlook calendar?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides event search with Outlook list events, calendar view, filters, sorting, and selected fields.

faq.question: Can it modify existing events?
faq.answer: Yes. It first resolves the event identifier, then updates only the fields the user requests.

faq.question: Will attendees receive email notifications?
faq.answer: They may. Creating, updating, deleting, or declining meetings can send Outlook notifications.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown workflow guide for using Outlook tools through Rube MCP.
